data.name: Settings_Sections
data.comment: Accessible label of the settings tabs

data.name: Settings_LanguageHint
data.value: Takes effect at the next start. Enum names from the C# project keep the language of its resources.

data.name: Settings_LanguageAfterRestart
data.value: FerretSharp shows the selected language after a restart.

data.name: Settings_ConnectionGroupHint
data.value: Shows a connection's group in front of its name in the connection switcher, the open and recent connections, the schema comparison and the confirmations, e.g. {0} – helpful when several groups have a DEV, TEST or PROD.

data.name: Settings_ExplorerViews
data.value: Views as a section of their own

data.name: Settings_ExplorerViewsHint
data.value: The explorer lists views and materialized views in a section of their own – Tables | Views | PL/SQL – instead of with the tables. The name search still names the hits in the other sections.

data.name: Settings_DataView
data.comment: Settings section: the grid of a table and the result of a query

data.name: Settings_HeaderTypesHint
data.value: Shows a column's Oracle type, e.g. {0}, under its name in the column header – in the grid of a table and in the result of a query.

data.name: Settings_HeaderNotNullHint
data.value: Marks the columns that must have a value. With the type off as well, the header loses this line and gets lower.

data.name: Settings_FilterSqlHint
data.value: What “SQL” in the filter bar shows and opens in the SQL editor: the grid's own statement – ROWID, each column, LOBs as preview and length, the first page – or {0} with the filter and the sorting only.

data.name: Settings_FilterSqlListed
data.comment: Option of "SQL of a filter"; the other option is "SELECT t.*"

data.name: Settings_ThemeForced
data.value: This session was started with {0} and therefore stays {1}. The selection is saved and applies from the next start without this parameter.
data.comment: {0} = the command line argument (code), {1} = Settings_ThemeForcedDark or Settings_ThemeForcedLight

data.name: Settings_ClrNamesHint
data.value: Entity and property names of the linked project in the explorer, the table header and the column search: beside the Oracle names, or in front in their place. FerretSharp always shows enum values with their C# name; SQL keeps the names of the database.

data.name: Settings_KeepAliveHint
data.value: Sends a short query to idle sessions every 2 minutes ({0}). A lost connection is reported immediately, and firewalls do not drop idle connections. Also checks shortly after the computer wakes from sleep. However, this keeps sessions open despite an {1} limit of the database.

data.name: Settings_LockWaitHint
data.value: If another session holds a lock on a row you want to write, FerretSharp waits this long and then shows who holds it ({0}).

data.name: Settings_FkCountsHint
data.value: The cell menu and the form show how many rows refer to the row. The counts run one after the other on the workspace’s session – a jump to another table waits until the running count has ended. “On hover” counts only the entry the mouse rests on.

data.name: Settings_FkCountsImmediately
data.comment: Option of "Count incoming foreign keys": all at once when the menu opens

data.name: Settings_FkCountsOnHover
data.comment: Option of "Count incoming foreign keys": only the entry under the mouse

data.name: Settings_DiagnoseUiStallsHint
data.value: Writes to the log when the user interface does not respond for more than 0.3 s, and what FerretSharp was busy with. If the .NET tool {0} is installed, stalls over 1.5 s also write the stacks of all threads to the log folder as {1}. Meant for tracking down stalls, not for everyday use.

data.name: Settings_NotRead
data.comment: Notice at start; the details (file, copy) follow as a warning

data.name: Shortcuts_Intro
data.value: Changes take effect at once. Click “Change” and press the new key combination; Esc cancels. Shortcuts use Ctrl, Alt or a function key; grayed-out ones are fixed.

data.name: Shortcuts_Changed
data.comment: A shortcut that differs from the default

data.name: Shortcuts_Change
data.comment: Button: record a new key combination

data.name: Shortcuts_Conflict
data.value: {0} is already assigned to “{1}” – applying removes it there.
data.comment: {0} = key combination, {1} = the action it is assigned to

data.name: Shortcuts_Fixed
data.comment: A shortcut that cannot be changed

data.name: Shortcuts_ResetAllQuestion
data.value: Reset all shortcuts to the defaults? A connection that has a default key loses it.

data.name: Settings_AuditTemplate
data.comment: Settings row: the file of the audit template

data.name: Settings_AuditSyncInDesigner
data.value: Bring audit up to date in the designer

data.name: Settings_AuditSyncInDesignerHint
data.value: When a table has an audit table, the table designer starts with “Bring audit table and trigger up to date” ticked: changed columns go into the audit table and trigger in the same script. Off: the box starts unticked. Opened from the audit line above the columns, it is ticked either way.

data.name: Settings_AuditTemplateHint
data.value: Audit table and trigger of a table follow this template – e.g. a file in your company's repository. It applies to every connection without a template of its group or its own. Empty uses the built-in template.

data.name: Settings_AuditTemplateFilter
data.comment: File type label in the open dialog

data.name: Settings_AuditTemplateReset
data.comment: Button: back to the built-in template

data.name: Settings_AuditTemplateUsingBuiltIn
data.value: The built-in template is used: audit table AUDIT_<table>, trigger <table>_AUDIT.

data.name: Settings_AuditTemplateCopyTitle
data.value: As the start of your own template – its syntax is explained in it

data.name: Settings_ShowDisplayNamesHint
data.value: Shows the value of the referenced table's display column beside a foreign key value in the grid, e.g. {0}. Mark a display column in the context menu of a column header.

data.name: Settings_DisplayColumnsFile
data.comment: Settings row: the file of the display columns

data.name: Settings_DisplayColumnsFileHint
data.value: Where the display columns are kept – e.g. in your team's repository, so colleagues see the same names. Empty uses a file in FerretSharp's data folder.

data.name: Settings_DisplayColumnsDefault
data.comment: Placeholder of the empty path field

data.name: Settings_DisplayColumnsFilter
data.comment: File type label in the open dialog

data.name: Settings_DisplayColumnsReset
data.comment: Button: back to the file in the data folder

data.name: Settings_DisplayColumnsResetTitle
data.value: Keep the display columns in FerretSharp's data folder again

data.name: Settings_DisplayColumnsNoFile
data.value: {0} does not exist yet: marking the first display column creates it.

data.name: Settings_Version
data.comment: Label of the installed version in Settings › Updates

data.name: Settings_VersionInstalled
data.value: Installed – updates come from the GitHub releases.

data.name: Settings_VersionNotInstalled
data.value: Not installed (a build or the zip): updates only reach a FerretSharp installed with Setup.exe.

data.name: Settings_CheckForUpdatesHint
data.value: At start and while FerretSharp runs (below), asks GitHub whether a newer version is out and shows it in the status bar. Downloading and installing wait for your click.

data.name: Settings_UpdateCheckInterval
data.comment: Label: how often to check for updates again while the app is open

data.name: Settings_UpdateCheckIntervalHint
data.value: Checks again this long after the last check, for when FerretSharp stays open for days. Only with automatic checks on.

data.name: Settings_Search
data.comment: Placeholder of the search field above the list of sections (WP-34)

data.name: Settings_ShortcutGroupInSearch
data.comment: Heading of a group of shortcuts among the search results of the settings (WP-34); {0}: the group, e.g. Editing

data.name: Settings_LinkProtocol
data.comment: Settings row: which FerretSharp opens ferretsharp:// links

data.name: Settings_LinkProtocolHint
data.value: A click on a ferretsharp:// link – from a colleague, in a ticket – opens the table in FerretSharp, after asking. The installer registers this itself; a portable copy or a build of your own does it here. Only for your Windows user.

data.name: Settings_LinkProtocolTakeOver
data.comment: Button: links open with this copy instead of another one

data.name: Settings_LinkProtocolNone
data.value: Links do not open with FerretSharp yet.

data.name: Settings_LinkProtocolFailed
data.value: The registration could not be changed: {0}

data.name: Settings_AuditTemplateGroupsHint
data.value: Each group of systems can have its own template, e.g. from its repository. A group without one takes the template above.

data.name: Settings_AuditTemplateNoGroups
data.value: No connection has a group yet – it is set in the connection dialog.

data.name: Settings_AuditTemplateGroupOrphaned
data.value: No connection is in this group any more (renamed?).

data.name: Settings_AuditTemplateAsGlobal
data.comment: Placeholder of a group's empty path field

data.name: Settings_AuditTemplateUseGlobal
data.comment: Button: the group takes the global template again

data.name: Settings_AuditTemplateAsGlobalTitle
data.value: The group takes the template above again

data.name: Settings_AuditTemplateRemove
data.comment: Button: removes the entry of a group no connection has

data.name: Settings_AuditTemplateOfGroup
data.comment: Accessible name of the path field. {0}: group name

data.name: Settings_AuditTemplateConnectionsHint
data.value: A connection whose audit tables follow another template than its group has its own, set in the connection dialog. It goes before the group's.

data.name: Settings_AuditTemplateNoConnections
data.value: No connection has its own template.

data.name: Settings_CodeEditorHint
data.value: Where a use of a column in the code opens ("Usage" view of a table). Visual Studio: the running instance that has the solution open, at the line; without one, a new window. VS Code at the line, or the program Windows opens .cs files with.

data.name: Settings_AutoReconnectHint
data.value: Connects a lost connection again by itself and restores its workspaces where you are – also one in the background. While the network or the database is away, it tries again for up to {0} min. If a workspace of the connection had uncommitted changes, the banner shows the loss as before. Workspaces unlocked for writing are read-only again.

data.name: Settings_AuditHighlightChangesHint
data.value: The grid of an audit table tints the values that differ from the version before and marks inserts and deletes – as the template says with @version-order and @action. Costs one query more per 500 rows, on the audit table by the base table's key: off for very large audit tables without an index on it.

data.name: Shortcuts_ConnectionsHint
data.value: A connection gets its shortcut in its dialog (Edit). The key shows the connection from anywhere in FerretSharp, connecting it first if needed.
